claims.statement: For every finite ordinary tree, every original leaf v with support s, and every integer rank p, I_{T-v}=I_H+zI_R and therefore g_v + Delta_p(T-v)=i_{p+1}(H)-i_{p-1}(H). In particular, at p=alpha(T)-2 each favorable summand equals i_{alpha-1}(H)-i_{alpha-3}(H)+|Delta_{alpha-2}(T-v)|.
claims.scope: All finite ordinary trees and original leaves; no residual or eligibility hypothesis is needed for the identities.
claims.reason: The independent-set split according to whether the support is selected proves the polynomial factorization; coefficient comparison proves the identities. No formal gate was assigned.

claims.statement: The frozen target at p=alpha-2 would follow from the pointwise rank-budget inequality i_{alpha-3}(H_v)-i_{alpha-1}(H_v) >= -Delta_{alpha-2}(T-v) on every favorable original leaf; this inequality is not proved here.
claims.scope: Eligible finite ordinary trees at the frozen p=alpha-2 rank.
claims.reason: The exact identity reduces each favorable summand to the difference in this inequality, but neither the pointwise budget nor a weaker aggregate budget has been established.

claims.statement: The stronger conjecture that every favorable summand is nonpositive at p=alpha-2 survived exact-DP checks on P_501, T_125, and four deterministic uniform Prüfer trees of order 260; all six were eligible and had zero positive favorable summands.
claims.scope: Six named constructed or deterministic random examples only.
claims.reason: Exact integer tree-DP replay; bounded evidence does not prove the candidate or the complete aggregate universally.

limitations: The frozen complete aggregate is not proved or refuted.
The pointwise rank-budget inequality and any aggregate substitute remain unproved.
The larger constructed and seeded Prüfer checks are bounded falsification attempts only.
